issues.legal_issue: A direction to pay for a tenant’s superstructure made outside the statutory compensation procedure does not trigger automatic dismissal of an ejectment suit for failure to pay within the statutory period.
material_facts: An ejectment decree had been passed before the tenant-protection legislation was extended to the town, and it remained unexecuted when the legislation became applicable.
The tenants’ applications seeking statutory relief were dismissed in their entirety as time-barred, and that dismissal became final.
The executing court nevertheless directed the decree-holders, on equitable grounds, to pay the reasonable value of the superstructure; the amount was assessed and time to deposit it was granted.
The decree-holders did not deposit the assessed amount within the initial period granted, but later deposited it within an extended period.
The lower courts treated the payment direction as one made under the statutory compensation procedure and held that the ejectment suit had automatically been dismissed.
issues.conclusion: The payment direction was made outside the Act, not under its statutory compensation procedure. The statutory automatic-dismissal provision therefore did not apply, and the ejectment suit had not stood dismissed for failure to deposit the amount within three months.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 10(1) and 10(2) of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921, where an ejectment decree had already been passed and remained unexecuted when the Act applied, the procedure in section 4 could be invoked through a tenant’s application for ascertainment of compensation and a fresh decree. Section 3 was not made applicable to such proceedings by section 10(1). Section 4(4)’s automatic-dismissal consequence applies to an order made under section 4, not to an equitable payment direction made after the statutory applications have been dismissed. V.K.A. Ranganatha Konar v. The Tiruchirappalli Municipal Council establishes that section 4(4) is mandatory for a decree under section 4 even if it does not expressly state the statutory payment period; G. Muthuvelu Pillai v. Hazarath Syed Shah Mian Sakkaf Sahib Khadiri Thaikal supports treating a payment direction for a superstructure as outside the Act where it is not made under the Act.

predicates.ejectment_decree_execution_proceeding: A landlord is pursuing execution of an ejectment decree that was passed before the relevant tenant-protection procedure became applicable.
predicates.statutory_compensation_application_dismi: The tenant’s application seeking the statutory compensation procedure was dismissed, and that dismissal became final.
predicates.equitable_superstructure_payment_order: The court directed payment for the tenant’s superstructure on equitable grounds rather than as part of the statutory compensation procedure.
predicates.ejectment_suit_not_automatically_dismiss: The ejectment suit remains undismissed by the statutory automatic-dismissal mechanism.

issues.definition: When execution of an ejectment decree involves a finally dismissed statutory compensation application and a separate equitable payment direction for a superstructure, the suit is not automatically dismissed for non-payment under the statutory procedure.
